summary: x402 moves signed stablecoin payments and has no identity, KYC or sanctions layer of its own, so regulation lands on the parties: stablecoin issuers, facilitators that broadcast payments, and sellers that receive them. The open questions are whether a non-custodial facilitator counts as a money transmitter or payment service provider (existing guidance does not address it directly), who screens for sanctions and carries travel-rule data, and how consumer-protection rules written for bank accounts apply to wallet transfers. Rows are dated; check each source before you rely on it.

rows.text: The protocol has no KYC, know-your-agent or sanctions layer. The CDP facilitator runs OFAC and Know Your Transaction checks on payments; other facilitators vary.

OFAC guidance for the virtual currency industry (2021-10-15) says sanctions duties apply to virtual currency businesses, penalties are generally strict liability, and screening should be risk-based. Facilitators and sellers each need their own view of this.

FinCEN guidance FIN-2019-G001 (2019-05-09) treats intermediaries by their control over value, and calls hosted wallet providers money transmitters. It does not address a non-custodial relayer that only broadcasts a payer-signed transfer, so how it applies to x402 facilitators is an open inference.
The GENIUS Act (Public Law 119-27, 2025-07-18) regulates payment stablecoins such as USDC and takes effect on the earlier of 2027-01-18 or 120 days after final regulations.
As of 2026-10-11 only proposed GENIUS Act rules were found (the OCC proposal of 2026-03-02); press reports say the 2026-07-18 rulemaking deadline passed without final rules.

Regulation E protects consumers against unauthorized transfers from accounts held at financial institutions, and the CFPB withdrew its 2025 proposal on emerging payment mechanisms (effective 2025-05-15). Whether it covers an x402 stablecoin wallet transfer is unclear, and exact payments have no protocol refund.
Products built on x402 add their own gates: the Cloudflare Monetization Gateway closed beta is limited to eligible US sellers and buyers, and Stripe's preview was reported as US only.
MiCA (Regulation (EU) 2023/1114) has applied to e-money tokens since 2024-06-30 and in full since 2024-12-30; the transitional period for crypto-asset service providers ended on 2026-07-01.

The Transfer of Funds Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 has applied the travel rule to crypto-asset transfers since 2024-12-30. x402 headers carry no originator or beneficiary data, so any travel-rule data must come from the service providers involved.

AI Act transparency duties under Article 50 apply from 2026-08-02; the Digital Omnibus (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744) moved Annex III high-risk obligations to 2027-12-02. Nothing in the AI Act is specific to agent payments.

GDPR covers information about an identifiable person, including online identifiers. Resource URLs, descriptions and payer addresses linked to a person that x402 sends to a facilitator can be personal data.

PSD3 and the Payment Services Regulation reached provisional agreement on 2025-11-27 and were listed as close to adoption on 2026-09-20, not yet in the Official Journal. They target payment service providers; x402 stablecoin payments sit mainly under MiCA instead.
The FCA published its cryptoasset regime policy statements on 2026-06-30, including stablecoin issuance (PS26/10); the full set of regulated activities applies from 2027-10-25.
Since 2023-09-01 UK cryptoasset businesses must apply the travel rule, and the FCA expects them to stay responsible even when they use third-party suppliers.

The FCA payments priorities report (2026-03-25) says it will consider whether regulation must change for agentic AI payments, and HM Treasury consulted on modernising payment services regulation from 2026-07-14 to 2026-10-06, naming agentic payments.

The Stablecoin Act in Bill C-15 received Royal Assent on 2026-03-26; the Bank of Canada will register and supervise non-bank fiat-backed stablecoin issuers, with the framework expected to take effect in 2027.
FINTRAC treats transferring virtual currency for clients as a money services business activity that needs registration, including for foreign businesses serving people in Canada.
The Retail Payment Activities Act brought payment service providers under Bank of Canada supervision on 2025-09-08 (risk management and safeguarding of funds).
Digital payment token services need a MAS licence under the Payment Services Act 2019, and MAS finalised a framework for single-currency stablecoins issued in Singapore on 2023-08-15.
MAS issued Guidelines on AI Risk Management for financial institutions on 2026-10-07, effective 2027-10-07, mentioning agentic AI systems that act autonomously.

Card-network rules do not apply to exact stablecoin settlements. The x402 Foundation runs a card-acceptance working group, but no specification text exists yet; cloudflare:402 is credit billed by Cloudflare as merchant of record under its own terms.
No primary Visa or Mastercard rule on agent-specific disputes or liability shifts was found as of 2026-10-11; a Worldpay analysis says no liability shift exists yet for agentic transactions.
